terms.meaning: Kannadigas' movement to bring all Kannada areas, scattered under many rulers, into one state.
"Family priest of Karnataka": the title given to Alur Venkata Rao in 1941.
The Fazal Ali Committee (with H. N. Kunzru and K. M. Panikkar) that redrew states by language in 1955.
A quarrel with a neighbour state over Kannada-majority areas left outside Karnataka.

items.name: Kannada land in Kavirajamarga
items.formula: It stretched from the Cauvery to the Godavari.
items.example: After Vijayanagara fell, Kannada areas came under more than 20 administrations.

items.name: The 20 administrative units
items.formula: Madras-Karnataka, Mumbai-Karnataka, Coorg, cantonments, Mysore and Hyderabad, plus 14 small provinces.

items.name: Early organisations
items.formula: Karnataka Vidya Vardhaka Sangha (1890, first president R. H. Deshpande), Kannada Sahitya Parishat (1915), Karnataka Sabha (1916).
items.example: Venkata Rango Katti served the cause early.

items.name: Belagavi Congress session (1924)
items.formula: Huyilgol Narayan Rao sang "Udayavagali Namma Cheluva Kannadanadu".

items.name: Alur Venkata Rao
items.formula: Asked "Where is Karnataka?" and wrote Past Glory of Karnataka with his own money.
items.example: Hyderabad Kannadigas called him Karnataka Kulapurohita in 1941.

items.name: Poets of unification
items.formula: Kuvempu: "Jayahe Karnataka Maate". Govinda Pai, the first Rashtrakavi, fought for Kasargod.
items.example: Shantakavi sang door to door to raise money for the Sahitya Sammelana.

items.name: Newspapers of the movement
items.formula: Bombay Karnataka: Vijaya, Rajahamsa, Kannada Kesari. Mysore: Suryodaya Prakashika, Hitabodhini.
items.example: Papers and books kept the movement alive.

items.name: First stage (1947-48)
items.formula: The 20 units were regrouped into five: Mumbai, Madras, Mysore, Hyderabad and Coorg.
items.example: The Constituent Assembly made A, B, C and D blocks, not language states.

items.name: Second stage (1953)
items.formula: Potty Sriramulu died after a 58-day fast; Andhra Pradesh was formed in 1953.
items.example: Seven taluks of Ballari joined Mysore; Chief Minister Kengal Hanumanthaiah backed unification.

items.name: Final stage (1956)
items.formula: On 1 November 1956 the unified state was formed as "Mysore State".
items.example: It joined old Mysore, Bombay and Hyderabad Kannada districts, Coorg, South Canara and Kollegal.

items.name: Mysore renamed Karnataka
items.formula: S. Nijalingappa was the first Chief Minister (1956).
items.example: On 1 November 1973, under D. Devaraj Urs, the state was named Karnataka.

items.name: Dispute with Maharashtra
items.formula: Over Belagavi, and Kannada areas like Akalkote, South Sholapur and Jat.
items.example: The Mahajan report (1966) kept Belagavi in Karnataka; the legislature meets yearly at Suvarna Soudha.

items.name: Dispute with Kerala
items.formula: Over Kasargod, once ruled by Kannada kings; Bekal fort was built by the Ikkeri kings.
items.example: The 1955 report gave it to Kerala; Kaiyara Kinhannarai kept the struggle alive.

mistakes.text: In 1956 the unified state was called Mysore State; the name Karnataka came only in 1973.
Nijalingappa was the first CM of the unified state; Kengal Hanumanthaiah was CM earlier, of the old state.
Ballari joined Mysore in 1953, when Andhra was formed, before the 1956 unification.
